title: Marine Analytics - latency, batching and hosting mode probe
summary: Discovery call to gather p95 latency targets, concurrency patterns, streaming token/sec profiles, and hosting preferences (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer runs a real-time marine sensor ingestion pipeline with short prompts and some long-form summarizations; wants a pilot for streaming telemetry and deterministic p95 under 250ms for short-turn prompts. Key concerns: multi-tenant noisy neighbors, data residency, KMS integration, and predictable cost for burst windows.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs
next steps for pilot and benchmarks

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Recording: auto
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Rina (Redwood SE), Lena (CTO - Marine Analytics), Paul (Lead ML Eng), Sam (SRE), Tobias (Product)

[00:00] Sofia Patel: Hey everyone thanks for hopping on. quick intros?
[00:07] Lena Ortiz: Hi yeah Lena here CTO at Marine Analytics, we're building real-time vessel telemetry insights, low-latency alerts matter.
[00:12] Paul Irving: Paul, ML, I own the model infra and inference tests.
[00:16] Sam Cho: Sam, SRE - throughput and bursting is my nightmare.
[00:20] Tobias Reed: Tobias product, curious about UX with streaming.
[00:24] Marco Diaz: Marco from Redwood, I'll cover batching/kv cache details.
[00:28] Rina Kapoor: Rina, solutions - I'll help with pilot ops.
[00:31] Sofia Patel: Great. high-level goal? Lena?
[00:35] Lena Ortiz: We need p95 sub-250ms for short prompts used in alerting paths, but for summarization flows p95 can be ~2s. We also have large bursts when a storm hits - token/sec spikes.
[00:49] Paul Irving: To add: most queries are 20-60 tokens but summaries go to 1k-2k tokens occasionally. average concurrent end-users typically 50-200, but bursts to 1k+ for 5-10 minutes.
[01:06] Marco Diaz: OK that distribution matters a lot. two axes: latency for short-turns and ability to accept high token/sec during bursts. are you planning hosted first?
[01:16] Lena Ortiz: Prefer to start hosted to move fast, but may need dedicated if noisy neighbor / p95 drift. private on prem later for EU regs.
[01:25] Sam Cho: Also need KMS support and audit logs - can't ship raw telemetry off without compliance controls.
[01:33] Sofia Patel: That's doable. Redwood Hosted supports KMS integrations and audit logs; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity so less noisy neighbor risk and better tail latency predictability.
[01:44] Paul Irving: Curious about the tradeoffs on cost - dedicated vs hosted for your typical profile.
[01:49] Marco Diaz: Cost is a function of reserved capacity vs usage. with hosted you pay per token but if bursts are frequent reserved/dedicated often cheaper per-token. we'll run some rough math after you share token histograms.
[02:04] Lena Ortiz: For SLA target, p95 250ms for short-turns, and 95th for summaries 2s is acceptable. can you get p95 250ms during a 1k concurrent burst?
[02:17] Marco Diaz: If you require deterministic 250ms at 1k concurrent, you'll likely need dedicated capacity with autoscale and burst pool. There are also batching strategies and prefix/KV cache to reduce token generation for repeated context. but 250ms at that concurrency for live streaming is aggressive.
[02:35] Paul Irving: What's the difference for streaming specifically? we want partial tokens as they arrive.
[02:40] Marco Diaz: Streaming adds small overhead per chunk but avoids waiting for full generation. key is continuous batching and low tail variance. for streaming we tune batch windows (e.g., 8-12ms) and use smaller kernels optimized for short sequences. but during bursts batching can actually improve throughput and maintain tail if configured.
[03:00] Sam Cho: What about KV cache / prefix caching - we have many repeated context like vessel id/profile.
[03:06] Rina Kapoor: Redwood can do prefix caching and KV cache hits reduce compute substantially. if typical prompts reuse the same few hundred tokens we can cache embeddings and key/values so p95 drops a lot.
[03:17] Paul Irving: How reliable is cache eviction during high churn? we can't accept stale context.
[03:22] Marco Diaz: Cache eviction is LRU with TTL options; we can pin critical prefixes for customers on Dedicated. on Hosted pinning depends on plan but we can recommend configuration.
[03:34] Lena Ortiz: Any specific hardware that gives best p95? we saw some providers pushing A100s, others on H100s.
[03:40] Marco Diaz: H100s can be better for larger seqs and quantized models; A100s still good for many workloads. Redwood runtime selects kernels per hardware and we publish performance profiles per model+hardware. we'll share our benchmark sheet.
[03:55] Tobias Reed: For our timeline: pilot in 2 weeks, production in 10-12 weeks is target. stakeholders: CTO, head of infra, ML lead.
[04:05] Sofia Patel: Next steps we'll propose: 48h hosted pilot with streaming enabled, we'll run your prompt set and measure p50/p95 and token/sec.
[04:12] Paul Irving: That works. Paul will provide anonymized prompt set.
[04:16] Sam Cho: We'll need an IP allowlist and SSO; is there a setup doc?
[04:20] Rina Kapoor: Yes we'll send onboarding checklist and SSO/KMS integration guide. link: https://redwood.ai/onboarding (placeholder) and security package.
[04:30] Paul Irving: can the hosted pilot simulate our burst pattern? we have a scheduled storm test next Tuesday.
[04:35] Marco Diaz: We'll run custom load generator based on your trace - token/sec and concurrency. expect to see p95 logged per route.
[04:42] Lena Ortiz: Also want to understand model quantization impacts on quality. we can't lose critical fields in summaries.
[04:47] Marco Diaz: We provide quantization profiles and a quality monitoring baseline. for dedicated you can pick a quantized variant but retain original as fallback and Redwood can automatically fallback if quality regression is detected.
[05:00] Tobias Reed: Any competitors we're worried about? we evaluated OtherCloudAI and a homegrown stack. main questions are cost and operational overhead.
[05:09] Sofia Patel: Right. Redwood's differentiation is predictable tail with dedicated and integrated tooling for rollouts + quality alerts. we'll demo the console during pilot.
[05:18] Paul Irving: On instrumentation - will you give us traces with token timestamps and KV hit rates?
[05:23] Marco Diaz: Yes, per-request breakdown, per-token latency histograms, batch sizes, and cache hit metrics.
[05:30] Sam Cho: SLA ask - can Redwood commit to p95 on hosted?
[05:34] Sofia Patel: Hosted has best-effort SLAs for tail; Dedicated gives stronger guarantees and SLA add-ons. we can propose a dedicated SLA if committed.
[05:43] Lena Ortiz: For pilot acceptance criteria: p95 < 250ms for 95% of short-turn routes in our simulated 5 minute bursts; streaming remains below x ms for first token and continues under threshold.
[05:55] Marco Diaz: We'll quantify first-token latency and ongoing token delta; also run steady-state 1 hour test to observe model heating and KV cache behavior.
[06:05] Paul Irving: sounds good. can you include cost projection for moving from hosted into reserved dedicated with our burst profile?
[06:11] Sofia Patel: yes - action items capture that.
[06:14] Tobias Reed: ok wrapping up, please include security docs and a simple pilot runbook.
[06:18] Sofia Patel: we'll send pricing, pilot plan and a short benchmark harness by Monday.
[06:22] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone, looking forward to the pilot.
[06:25] Sofia Patel: thanks - we'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff and the storm test runbook.
[06:30] (end recording)
